historical_references.reference: Devabrata was the name of a celebrated sage and a great devotee of Lord Vishnu. He was the elder brother of Bhishma, the grandsire of the Pandava princes in the Mahabharata epic. Devabrata, also known as Bhagiratha, performed the Tripada Yajna (a sacred fire ritual) to bring the Gods of the Himalayas to the Gangasagar Island, so that the ashes of his ancestor King Sagara could be immersed in the holy waters of the Ganga, thereby freeing them from the curse of the sage Kapila.

Devabrata was also a king in ancient India, who ruled over the kingdom of Anga in the eastern part of the Indian subcontinent. He was a contemporary of the Buddha, and is mentioned in various Buddhist scriptures as a powerful king who was an ardent follower of Buddhism and built many viharas (monasteries) to accommodate the monks and nuns. According to one legend, Devabrata was visited by the Buddha himself during one of his travels and was deeply moved by the Buddha's teachings, and henceforth became a devoted disciple and an important supporter of Buddhism.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Devabrata' is derived from Sanskrit words 'Deva' which means God and 'Brata' which means vow. In contemporary culture, this name is found in various modern contexts across three distinct platforms: Bollywood movies, Indian spirituality blogs, and technology startups. In Bollywood movies, characters with the name Devabrata are often depicted as spiritual, god-fearing individuals, such as in the film 'Dev.D'. Indian spirituality blogs often feature blogs or articles about individuals named Devabrata, who are spiritual leaders or gurus. In the technology startup ecosystem, the name Devabrata can be seen in companies or founders who aim to embody the spiritual values of truth, wisdom, and devotion in their work.
